A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DaWin study and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. v2 retains the original material while expanding Appendix A.3.

before.justification: v1 reports original CLIP classification experiments, model-merging comparisons, ablations, and runtime analyses in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds coefficient-optimality, calibration, computational-cost, and model-pool analyses.

M1.justification: Table F introduces a parallel inference variant that evaluates the pretrained and fine-tuned models simultaneously on multiple GPUs during expertise estimation. The coefficient formulas, offset adjustment, mixture modeling, and task-vector formulation remain unchanged. Temperature scaling was already documented in v1 Appendix A.2.3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet and its five distribution-shift benchmarks plus the same eight multitask datasets. The added analyses reuse this coverage; Table G changes candidate-model configurations rather than datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 substantially expands direct coefficient-rule comparisons beyond v1's pseudo-label alternatives. Table D and Figure H evaluate uniform random coefficients, two Gaussian rules, maximum-logit ratios, confidence ratios, and confidence-difference ratios. The original benchmark comparator sets remain intact.

E3.justification: The original evaluation settings are retained, but v2 adds several distinct protocols: per-sample coefficient search over 0.05–0.95 with MSE evaluation, MMD/FID dataset-distance measurements, calibration removal, controlled candidate-model pools, and resource profiling including parallel inference. These are additional evaluation designs, not evidence that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds tests of oracle-coefficient optimality, alternative coefficient generators, calibration sensitivity, computational tradeoffs, and interference from nonexpert models. Figures G–H additionally examine dataset similarity and the entropy-valley hypothesis. The earlier offset, sample-size, correlation, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, performance confidence intervals, or significance testing. Table C's new standard deviations describe variation of optimal coefficients across samples, rather than uncertainty in experimental performance estimates.

E6.justification: The original result tables remain unchanged, while Tables C–G and Figures G–H add substantial diagnostic results. Table E reports calibrated versus uncalibrated DaWin accuracies of 78.7/54.4 versus 76.6/54.0 for ID/OOD. Table C also reveals an exception to coefficient superiority: on ImageNet-V2, X-entropy-ratio MSE is 0.1559 versus 0.1390 for the WiSE-FT constant.

T1.justification: The interpolation equations, mixture-model derivations, entropy-valley hypotheses, and expert-weighting lemma and proof are retained. Lemma 6.1 and its Appendix A.4 restatement are condensed and reformatted without changing their mathematical assumptions or conclusions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: training-free entropy-based dynamic interpolation, efficient mixture modeling, and improved robust adaptation across 14 classification tasks. The added analyses support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes label-informed oracle coefficients from guaranteed optima and removes the 'optimal-like' description in Table 6. It adds interpretations concerning calibration dependence and interference from nonexpert models, and connects the inference-cost tradeoff to test-time scaling in Appendix A.5.

D1.justification: New analyses disclose NVIDIA A100 hardware, concurrent multi-GPU expertise evaluation, CLIP and Inception V3 feature extractors for dataset distances, and the coefficient-search grid. Existing checkpoint sources, mixture settings, calibration instructions, and code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting test-time scaling, multimodal distribution-shift limitations, and model-interpolation motivation, including Snell et al., Muennighoff et al., and Model Ratatouille. Section 5 and the central positioning against static merging and training-dependent dynamic methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes include localized clarification of oracle terminology and calibration, shorter lemma statements, corrected cross-references, revised acknowledgments, and the ICLR 2025 publication header. The main narrative and section organization remain stable; substantive additions primarily extend Appendix A.3.

P2.justification: v2 adds dataset-distance heatmaps and broader entropy-comparison plots in Figures G–H, together with five new diagnostic and comparison tables, C–G. Existing displays are retained, and the proof and limitations follow the expanded empirical appendix.

improvement.justification: The added coefficient controls, calibration ablation, and model-pool analysis strengthen the justification for existing design choices. Clarifying that oracle coefficients are not guaranteed optima improves interpretive precision, and Table F makes resource tradeoffs more explicit. These are useful refinements, although Table F leaves unclear why parallel execution reduces the reported FLOPs per sample.
